subject: Growth commit kickoff: timeline, MAP, and QBR windows
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Ramirez <alex@starlit.ai>, Priya Shah <priya@starlit.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Growth commit kickoff: timeline, MAP, and QBR windows

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the conversation last week. Per our call, Starlit is targeting a +40% throughput uplift and a license increase from 120 to 200 seats starting Jan 1, 2027. To get ahead of exec approvals, I wanted to kick off a short mutual action plan and lock a couple QBR windows so we can review capacity, routing, and the proposed term adjustments.

Attached: Starlit_MAP_v2.xlsx (MAP with milestones), SLA-exception-request.pdf (one small SLO tweak request).

High-level proposed timeline
- Oct 5–12: finalize MAP and pricing/term ask (Marissa / Alex)
- Oct 13–22: legal & procurement review (Starlit + Redwood legal)
- Nov 1: internal exec signoff target
- Jan 1, 2027: new seats live; dedicated capacity allocation effective

QBR windows (pick one):
- Nov 9–10, 2026 (Tue–Wed) between 10:00–12:00 PT
- Nov 16–17, 2026 (Tue–Wed) between 13:00–16:00 PT

Immediate asks:
1) Alex/Priya — confirm which QBR window works and whether procurement needs a clean PO before DocuSign.
2) Ben/Tessa — I flagged a potential 10% promotional credit for the first 6 months (requested by Starlit). Can legal/finance confirm if that's feasible?

If those two QBR slots don't work, suggest 1–2 dates and we'll adjust.

Thanks — looking forward to a quick turnaround so we can begin capacity planning.

Best,
Marissa
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Starlit_MAP_v2.xlsx (Excel, 42KB), SLA-exception-request.pdf (PDF, 18KB)

From: Alex Ramirez <alex@starlit.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@starlit.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Growth commit kickoff: timeline, MAP, and QBR windows

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear plan and for sending the MAP. Nov 16–17 (afternoon PT) works best for our team — Priya and I are available on the 17th between 13:00–15:00 PT.

Quick notes from procurement side: Starlit prefers to sign a DocuSign first and follow up with a PO for internal accounting. The pricing ask in the MAP looks good but I need to confirm one line item: the dedicated GPU pool uplift. Can you confirm whether the stated uplift assumes preemptible capacity or reserved GPU slices? That will determine how we budget.

We are open to the 10% promotional credit on first 6 months — happy to have Ben loop in for a short pricing chat.

Thanks — looking forward to the QBR.

—Alex
Head of Platform Engineering
Starlit AI

Subject: Re: Growth commit kickoff: timeline, MAP, and QBR windows

Alex — great, thanks for confirming the 17th window. We'll lock Nov 17, 2026 from 13:00–15:00 PT for the QBR and send a calendar invite after Ben and Tessa confirm the availability on our side.

To answer your capacity question: the MAP's dedicated GPU uplift assumes reserved slices (non-preemptible) to guarantee latency SLOs for inference. Ben — please confirm sizing and whether we should propose a burst pool for peak hours.

Next steps
- Marissa: send calendar invite + HubSpot deal update (today)
- Ben: confirm exact reserved GPU sku and pricing delta (by Oct 8)
- Tessa: prep a short capacity runbook and capacity-cost breakdown for the QBR (by Nov 3)
- Alex/Priya: confirm DocuSign flow vs PO preference (this week)

I'll attach an updated MAP after Ben confirms numbers.

Best,
Marissa

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, 07 Oct 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Growth commit kickoff: timeline, MAP, and QBR windows

Quick note — I reviewed the MAP and the reserved slice plan. We can support the capacity uplift with a 2x reserved slice + small burst pool (estimated delta: $18k/month).

Promotional credit: finance can approve a 10% credit for the first 6 months if Starlit signs an 18-month term (vs standard 12). Document-wise, legal will want that in the term amendment and we should draft a short addendum.

I'll draft the pricing line items and push an updated MAP by Oct 8 EOD.

Ben
Senior Sales Manager
Redwood Inference
